name: Alder Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds alaska to northeastern usa; winters colombia to bolivia
description: Small flycatcher, extremely similar to several other species. Prefers clearings and boggy areas, often with patches of alders.

name: Japanese Wagtail
rangeDescription: Breeds japanese islands; winters to china, korea, and taiwan
description: Large, boldly patterned, long-tailed songbird of waterside areas, particularly fast-flowing streams but also rivers, pools, inland lakes, and coastal areas. Adult male velveteen black with white belly, wings, throat, brow, and outer tail feathers.

name: Lesser Seedcracker
rangeDescription: Eastern tanzania to southern malawi, eastern zimbabwe, and northern mozambique
description: A colorful, chunky waxbill with a large conical bill. Both sexes have a red hood and tail, but females have slightly less extensive red.

name: Semipalmated Plover
rangeDescription: Breeds northern north america; winters to southern south america and hawaiian islands
description: Small, orange-legged plover with solid dark breast band. Medium-brown upperparts are the color of wet sand, noticeably darker than Piping or Snowy Plovers.

name: Shaft-tailed Whydah
rangeDescription: Southern angola to namibia, zambia, botswana, southern mozambique, and kwazulu-natal
description: A small whydah with a reddish-orange bill and legs. The breeding male has buffy-orange underparts and neck, a dark cap, and 17-centimeter-long black tail feathers.

name: White-throated Grasswren
rangeDescription: Sandstones of central arnhem land, northern territory
description: Distinctive long-tailed, chestnut-and-black bird with a stark white throat, found only in the western Arnhem Plateau of Northern Territory, in areas with large spinifex clumps around large sandstone boulders. Frequent burning of these areas has made this species very hard to find, and it is no longer reliably seen in accessible locations.
imageCreditName: Laurie Ross | Tracks Birding & Photography Tours

name: Striped Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (central queensland to northwestern victoria and southeastern south australia)
description: Medium-sized honeyeater with distinctive streaking. Underparts white, upperparts primarily gray.

name: Kirtland's Warbler
rangeDescription: Jack-pine area of michigan; winters in bahamas
description: One of the largest and rarest warblers. Breeds only in young jack pine forests in northern Michigan and Wisconsin.

name: Himalayan Griffon
rangeDescription: Himalayas from northwestern india to tibet and west-central china
description: A regal raptor of steppes, valleys, and mountainous regions, this large scavenger is fairly common throughout most of its range. Adult is sandy brown with a pale, featherless head.

name: Santa Marta Woodstar
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Tiny bumblebee-like hummingbird found only in and around Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains, where it is the only woodstar. Usually encountered in cloud forest at moderate elevations, but occasionally wanders down to near sea level.

name: Friendly Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern borneo (mounts kinabalu and trus madi)
description: Though frequently derided for the reputed inaccuracy of its name, this mouse-like bird can prove quite confiding. It is, however, generally quite difficult to see in dense undergrowth; best detected by its song, a series of three piercing whistles, the last of which is long and grating.

name: Hume's Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern india, nepal, bhutan, and southeastern tibet
description: This dull, shy skulker can be difficult to see; instead, listen for its remarkable song, an ascending series of 3-4 long thin monotone whistles (“doooooo-rayyyyy-meeeee”) followed by a slow series of repeated 2- or 3-note musical phrases. If seen well, note the species’ white brow stripe, buff-washed pale underparts, and warm brown upperparts.

name: Campbell Islands Shag
rangeDescription: Campbell islands
description: A medium-sized, black-and-white marine shag with a metallic green-and-blue glimmer on the black head, neck, and throat. Note the white wing patches.

name: Campbell Islands Shag
rangeDescription: Campbell islands
description: A medium-sized, black-and-white marine shag with a metallic green-and-blue glimmer on the black head, neck, and throat. Note the white wing patches.

name: Pied Cuckoo-Dove
rangeDescription: Bismarck archipelago, including admiralty islands
description: A large silver and black cuckoo-dove that shows obvious contrast between the light silver chest, belly, neck, and head and the much darker gray wings and tail. More confined to primary foothill forest than other cuckoo-doves in its range, which are smaller and less robust, lacking the distinctive silver-gray color scheme of Pied.

name: Spanish Eagle
rangeDescription: Locally in iberian peninsula; formerly morocco
description: Rare eagle breeding only in Spain and Portugal, with some immatures dispersing into North Africa. Very similar to the closely-related Imperial Eagle, but is darker overall and adults have a distinctive white leading wing edge on the shoulders which can been seen from below when flying.

name: Scaled Pigeon
rangeDescription: Tropical southern mexico to brazil and northeastern argentina
description: Handsome large pigeon of humid forest and edge in tropical lowlands. Usually seen flying overhead, less often perched in canopy of tall trees.

name: White-naped Yuhina
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern india (assam) to myanmar and southern china (northwestern yunnan)
description: Exquisite yuhina with an orange head and crest with white ears and throat. Nape is not obviously pale, but the white “trim” to the back edge of the crest is noticeable.

name: Croaking Ground Dove
rangeDescription: Arid western ecuador, peru, and northern chile
description: Small, dirt-colored dove of desert lowlands, where it is often common in towns, parks, farmland, and semiopen areas in general. In pairs or small groups; feeds on the ground but often perches on wires.

name: Kauai Amakihi
rangeDescription: Humid montane ohia/koa forest of kauai
description: An uncommon Hawaiian honeycreeper of forests on Kauai. Males are bright yellow and females are grayer.
